rv.q: Josie Rourke’s production is ferocious but light on its feet.
This is an uneven but bold probing of a dirty little secret in society that finds, in Ambika Mod, an eloquent expression of underlying pain.
Anchored by Mod, Porn Play is by turns funny and disturbing – a welcome and bold addition to the growing discourse surrounding sex and the internet.
It’s a bold play with a fantastically committed performance from Mod.
The unfortunate upshot of this is that we, like everyone in Ani’s life, feel very distant from her.
Porn Play operates on a broader canvas but delivers a portrait of a woman who remains more symbol than substance.
Sophia Chetin-Leuner has written a brave play on a difficult subject: pornography.
The funny and unsettling new production, Porn Play, makes its world premiere at the Theatre, starring Ambika Mod (This is Going to Hurt, One Day).
Mod and the others turn a rather superficial script into a show that, for all its defects, is worth seeing.
But mostly this is an absorbing, witty, layered play: and Chetin-Leuner nails Milton and Eve as singular metaphors. A must-see.
I left Porn Play feeling incredibly satisfied by what I had witnessed, with not a drop of regret.
Porn Play is an interesting watch that made me not just think, but read the whole playtext through.

Chetin-Leuner establishes an engaging premise and delivers it with adequate deftness. Overall, the script is crafted with upbeat pacing, sharp dialogue, and perceptiveness. The text overflows (smirk) with interesting analysis of society’s codes and their understanding of relationships, love, and desire.

cn.t: Ambika Mod delivers a fearless performance in this bold but uneven exploration of pornography addiction. Critics praise its vital subject matter and striking staging, though some find the protagonist emotionally distant.
